requirements.requirement: Only one invocation processes pending.tsv at a time, and a concurrent invocation receives a clear result.
requirements.summary: A live owner held the nonblocking lock while a concurrent invocation exited 75 with an explicit already-running message; the ledger remained unchanged during the interrupted test.

requirements.requirement: Each pending batch ID reaches ledger.tsv exactly once while existing ledger entries are preserved.
requirements.summary: The original B100 entry was preserved, B101 and B102 were added, all three IDs had count 1, and a subsequent reconciliation left the ledger checksum unchanged.

requirements.requirement: An interrupted invocation must not permanently block later work.
requirements.summary: The active owner was terminated, after which a new invocation acquired the lock, completed successfully, and processed both pending IDs exactly once.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The implementation used the installed util-linux flock 2.23.2 and POSIX shell. Direct post-restart observations still showed RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also strong: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, restart scheduling followed by temporary unreachability, a different boot identity corroborated by fixed lifecycle observations, and recovered system, crond, script, ledger, and reconciliation state.
limitations: Package-manager health checks timed out both before and after execution, so package-database consistency was not independently verified.
Several executor-created temporary diagnostic and evidence files remained after completion, although they do not affect the demonstrated task functionality.

operational_hygiene.summary: The required script, ledger updates, bounded behavior tests, and mandatory restart had clear task or evidence roles. No failed services or new network exposure were observed. One unnecessary low-risk mutation occurred when a flawed process-discovery command created /tmp/reconcile.procs; it did not contribute because it matched its own command and remained after completion. Other purposeful prerequisite/evidence operations also left avoidable residue: /tmp/reconcile.pids, /tmp/reconcile-owner.out, /tmp/reconcile-contender.out, and /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log remained rather than being cleaned. The failed first installation attempt did not establish a managed-system mutation and was later corrected.
